messages:
maria: Quick question — we need to grant a contractor temporary console access to view logs for the training pipeline (project: redwood-training). They only need read access to the pipeline logs and we must ensure any PII is redacted. What's the least-privilege way to do this quickly? cc @sec-bot

aj: short answer: avoid project-level Viewer. give logging-only roles + ephemeral duration. if they need to use a sa, use short-lived tokens (STS) and limit SA perms.

leo: agree. options: 1) grant roles/logging.viewer at project or folder (but prefer project+log filter) 2) create a custom role with just logging.logEntries.list + logging.logs.list + bigquery.dataViewer if reading exports 3) use an ephemeral service account and bind it to the custom role for a short window.

samir: how long is "temporary" here? also where are logs stored — stackdriver vs bigquery sink? that affects perms and redaction approach.

maria: contractor needs access for about 4 hours to triage dataset labeling pipeline. logs land in Cloud Logging; we already have a BigQuery sink for longer retention but primary debugging will be in Logging console.

leo: for Cloud Logging console-only view, a minimal binding could be: `roles/logging.viewer` plus a condition to restrict to the training pipeline resource. if we want to redact fields, we should NOT grant access to raw BigQuery sink unless we ensure redaction at sink time.

aj: sample gcloud for ephemeral SA token (STS) — run from infra team side to mint creds for them:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding sa-ephemeral@redwood-training.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member="user:contractor@example.com" --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountUser" --condition="expression=request.time < timestamp('2023-08-01T12:00:00Z')",title="temp"
# then grant sa the custom logging role at project scope
```
this keeps the user identity out of project-level bindings.

sec-bot: Automated check: JIT access recommended. Please open a JIT request with duration and justification. See https://intra.redwood/security/jit for flow. Remember audit logs will capture the SA impersonation.

maria: That works. For redaction — can we rely on the existing sink to BigQuery with a redaction transform, or do we need to mask in Logging?

leo: best practice: add a log sink with a transform that removes PII before it reaches long-term storage. For console viewing, you can also apply Logging views with advanced filters that exclude sensitive fields. But console is not a guarantee — anyone with logging.viewer can pull raw entries unless we use a filtered view or a custom role that prevents reading certain labels (limited).

samir: action items: (1) infra create ephemeral SA + bind for 4h (2) security to review custom role json and ensure it doesn't include any bigquery read perms (3) contractor to use SA via STS and provide justification for audit. I'll open a quick PR template for the custom role. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — I'll open the JIT request and ping infra for the SA. tagging @aj to review the custom role when Samir posts the PR.

aj: will review. keep it to logging.* read-only and serviceAccountUser only. no broad roles.

leo: I'll double-check the sink redaction config and confirm if we need an extra transform.

maria: awesome, closing this thread after JIT + PR. thanks! :pray:
